scenes.visual: Title card: Equal Cells, One Winner.

scenes.tts: A small group of cells are all equal. Every one could become a nerve cell. Why does only one?
scenes.visual: A cluster of identical pale cells in a sheet. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: A small group of cells are all equal. Every one could become a nerve cell. Why does only one?

scenes.tts: In the fly embryo, the cells that will make the nervous system sit in small groups.
scenes.visual: Map 1: fly embryo in cross-section. The ectoderm, with the ventral neuroectoderm on the underside; small clusters lit there and elsewhere in the ectoderm.
scenes.narration: In the fly embryo, the cells that will make the nervous system sit in small groups.

scenes.tts: Every cell in a group can become a neural precursor. Yet usually only one does.
scenes.visual: One cluster zooms in: five equal cells, then one glows brighter.
scenes.narration: Every cell in a group can become a neural precursor. Yet usually only one does.

scenes.tts: If the cells start equal, something must break the tie.
scenes.visual: A balance scale between two identical cells.
scenes.narration: If the cells start equal, something must break the tie.

scenes.tts: The answer comes in two steps. First, proneural genes make a group of cells able to become neural.
scenes.visual: Step card 1: competence. The whole cluster tints.
scenes.narration: The answer comes in two steps. First, proneural genes make a group of cells able to become neural.

scenes.tts: Then the cells signal to each other through Notch, and one wins.
scenes.visual: Step card 2: selection. Arrows pass between cells; one cell stays bright.
scenes.narration: Then the cells signal to each other through Notch, and one wins.

scenes.tts: Keep three maps in mind. On the embryo's underside, one cell from each cluster moves inward as a neuroblast.
scenes.visual: Map 1 again: one cell from the cluster drops inward, labelled neuroblast.
scenes.narration: Keep three maps in mind. On the embryo's underside, one cell from each cluster moves inward as a neuroblast.

scenes.tts: A neuroblast is a neural stem cell of the fly embryo. The rest of the cluster becomes epidermis, the skin.
scenes.visual: The remaining cells flatten at the surface, labelled epidermis.
scenes.narration: A neuroblast is a neural stem cell of the fly embryo. The rest of the cluster becomes epidermis, the skin.

scenes.tts: On the notum, the back of the fly's thorax, small clusters make the large bristles. Each gives one sensory organ precursor.
scenes.caption: On the notum, the back of the fly's thorax, small clusters make the large bristles. Each gives one sensory organ precursor (SOP).
scenes.visual: Map 2: the fly notum with rows of large and small bristles. One small cluster gives one cell labelled SOP.
scenes.narration: On the notum, the back of the fly's thorax, small clusters make the large bristles. Each gives one sensory organ precursor (SOP).

scenes.tts: That cell builds one bristle and its neuron. The rest become epidermis. Small bristles come from broader stripes.
scenes.visual: The SOP grows into a bristle with a neuron at its base. In the background, a broad stripe gives many small-bristle precursors.
scenes.narration: That cell builds one bristle and its neuron. The rest become epidermis. Small bristles come from broader stripes.

scenes.tts: The third map is the vertebrate neural tube. There, the cells are already neural.
scenes.visual: Map 3: neural tube cross-section with dividing progenitors.
scenes.narration: The third map is the vertebrate neural tube. There, the cells are already neural.

scenes.tts: Now step one. A proneural gene first comes on in a whole cluster. Think of it as a casting call.
scenes.visual: Back to the embryo's ectoderm. A cluster lights up together. Label: casting call, everyone auditions.
scenes.narration: Now step one. A proneural gene first comes on in a whole cluster. Think of it as a casting call.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-three, Mar Ruiz Gomez and Alain Ghysen followed the proneural gene akeety in staged fly embryos.
scenes.caption: In 1993, Mar Ruiz-Gómez and Alain Ghysen followed the proneural gene achaete in staged fly embryos.
scenes.visual: Name card: Ruiz-Gómez and Ghysen, 1993. Staged embryos in a row.
scenes.narration: In 1993, Mar Ruiz-Gómez and Alain Ghysen followed the proneural gene achaete in staged fly embryos.

scenes.tts: It came on first in clusters of a few cells. Later, one cell in each cluster held much more akeety RNA.
scenes.visual: Time-lapse: the whole cluster stained, then one cell dark and the others fading.
scenes.narration: It came on first in clusters of a few cells. Later, one cell in each cluster held much more achaete RNA.
scenes.caption: It came on first in clusters of a few cells. Later, one cell in each cluster held much more achaete RNA.

scenes.tts: That cell became the neural progenitor. They called the first state competent, and the second determined.
scenes.visual: Two labels: competent over the cluster, determined over the single cell.
scenes.narration: That cell became the neural progenitor. They called the first state competent, and the second determined.

scenes.tts: Predict. Take Notch away from the embryo. What happens to the clusters?
scenes.visual: Prompt card: No Notch. What happens to the clusters? The embryo map with blank cluster positions.
scenes.narration: Predict. Take Notch away from the embryo. What happens to the clusters?

scenes.visual: Hold on the prompt. A small timer icon.

scenes.tts: The clusters still form in their normal places. But high akeety is no longer limited to one cell.
scenes.caption: The clusters still form in their normal places. But high achaete is no longer limited to one cell.
scenes.visual: Reveal: clusters appear in the usual spots; every cell in each cluster stays dark.
scenes.narration: The clusters still form in their normal places. But high achaete is no longer limited to one cell.

scenes.tts: So Notch does not place the clusters. It narrows them. Placing and picking are separate events.
scenes.visual: Two boxes: placing (regulatory DNA) and picking (Notch).
scenes.narration: So Notch does not place the clusters. It narrows them. Placing and picking are separate events.

scenes.tts: That leaves three puzzles. Who may become neural? Who does? And does the logic carry over to vertebrates?
scenes.visual: Three numbered puzzle cards: Who may? Who does? Does it carry over?
scenes.narration: That leaves three puzzles. Who may become neural? Who does? And does the logic carry over to vertebrates?

scenes.tts: Here is the idea to carry. In the fly, proneural factors say which cells may become neural. Notch says which one does.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: In the fly, proneural factors say who may. Notch says who does.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea to carry. In the fly, proneural factors say which cells may become neural. Notch says which one does.

scenes.visual: Hold on the takeaway card.
